name: How much rear yard do I need to keep after the addition?

mainEntity.name: After building a rear addition, how do I know whether enough open yard remains for zoning and practical use?
mainEntity.text: After building a rear addition, how do I know whether enough open yard remains for zoning and practical use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rear yard requirements are not just about passing code; they also affect how the house feels after construction. A project may technically fit on the lot while leaving the backyard too small to be practical. In many Los Angeles-area neighborhoods, homeowners also need to think about light, privacy, outdoor seating, drainage, and access to mechanical equipment. The usable yard can shrink quickly once walls, patios, stairs, and utility clearances are added. That is why a rear addition should be evaluated both as a zoning exercise and as a livability exercise. The best design leaves the yard large enough to support everyday use, not just the minimum allowed by code. Before moving ahead, homeowners should compare the proposed footprint against both the required open area and the kind of outdoor space they actually want to keep.
acceptedAnswer.description: The required amount of rear yard depends on zoning, lot size, and the type of addition. Even if a project technically fits, homeowners should leave enough usable open space for light, access, drainage, and future flexibility.
